case_title.quote: STATE OF RAJASTHAN v. MEHRAM & ORS.
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

number_of_accused.quote: All the five accused preferred appeal before the High Court
number_of_accused.reason: Five accused are named in the FIR and all five appealed.

accused_gender.reason: Judgment never states a gender category; accused are named male persons, so 'Mixed' has no support.

accused_age.reason: Age 70 is the lower bound; the judgment gives an approximate range of 70-75 years.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of the accused is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_occupation.reason: Accused occupation is not stated in the judgment.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Socioeconomic status of the accused is not stated.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No previous criminal record is mentioned in the judgment.

victim_gender.reason: Victim Bhura Ram is referred to with male name and pronouns; male is supported.

victim_age.reason: No age is given for the deceased anywhere in the judgment; 30 is unsupported.

victim_caste.reason: Victim caste is not mentioned in the judgment.

victim_religion.reason: Victim religion is not mentioned in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Neighbours/co-villagers in a dispute over a field passage
accused_victim_relationship.quote: There was a dispute between the parties for using the fields as a passage
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Parties were rival villagers in a land-passage dispute, not strangers.

offence_category.correct_value: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder (s.304 Part I); trial court had convicted for murder (s.302)
offence_category.quote: the case would be covered by Section 304 Part I, IPC
offence_category.reason: Murder was the trial court's charge, but the Supreme Court held the offence fell under s.304 Part I.

statutory_provisions.reason: Judgment cites s.149 not s.34, and no Arms Act provision is mentioned.

weapon.reason: Kassies and lathies are the weapons described in the judgment.

evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness and medical evidence are the main evidence relied on; recovery and spot memo also cited.

confession.reason: Judgment does not mention any confession, so 'None' is an unsupported inference.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Accused armed with lethal weapons, lay in wait, and struck a fatal blow with intention to kill
aggravating_circumstances.quote: The accused party armed with lethal weapons assaulted the complainant party
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Weapons and intent are supported; provocation was treated as mitigating, not aggravating.

mitigating_circumstances.correct_value: Grave and sudden provocation from repeated unauthorised entry on accused's fields; superficial injuries to accused
mitigating_circumstances.quote: deprived of the power of self-control by grave and sudden provocation
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Judgment expressly identifies grave and sudden provocation as a mitigating factor.

trial_court_outcome.quote: accused Mehram son of Chhagna is hereby held guilty of committing offence under Section 148, 302, 324/149 Indian Penal Code
trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court convicted under ss.148, 302, 324/149 and imposed life imprisonment.

high_court_outcome.quote: his conviction under Section 302 IPC is converted into one under Section 326 IPC
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court converted s.302 to s.326 and sentenced to period undergone.

final_outcome.quote: convicting the accused No. 5 ... for offence punishable under Section 304 Part I and Section 148, IPC
final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court convicted accused No. 5 under s.304 Part I and s.148.

offence_finally_established.quote: convicting the accused No. 5 ... for offence punishable under Section 304 Part I and Section 148, IPC
offence_finally_established.reason: s.304-I is the same as s.304 Part I; s.148 also upheld.

imprisonment_type.quote: sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for ten (10) years
imprisonment_type.reason: A fixed-term simple imprisonment of ten years was imposed.

imprisonment_years.quote: sentence of ten (10) years of simple imprisonment
imprisonment_years.reason: Ten years is the sentence imposed for s.304 Part I.

fine_rs.quote: and fine of Rs.100/- on each count
fine_rs.reason: Fine of Rs.100 on each count is stated.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Facts as stated, but intent to kill and aggressor status are contested findings, not established facts; no outcome should be implied
neutral_facts.quote: The victim sustained fatal injuries from a single blow to the head, which was intentional.
neutral_facts.reason: Presents contested intent and aggressor findings as settled facts, edging toward the court's conclusion.

offence_severity.correct_value: Not stated for s.304 Part I; s.326 punishable with life or up to ten years
offence_severity.quote: punishable with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years
offence_severity.reason: No minimum of 10 years is stated; ten years is a maximum for s.326 in the judgment.

attempt_completion.quote: the death of the victim was caused by the one fatal blow
attempt_completion.reason: Offence resulted in death, so completed offence is supported.

physical_harm.quote: brain injury and due to the injury No. 1
physical_harm.reason: Doctor's opinion attributes death to brain injury from the head blow.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Accused No. 5 convicted of two offences: s.304 Part I and s.148 IPC
number_of_offences.quote: convicting the accused No. 5 ... for offence punishable under Section 304 Part I and Section 148, IPC
number_of_offences.reason: No upheld-count of 'one'; two convictions were recorded for accused No. 5.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property loss is at issue; compensation is not property loss.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Accused assembled with lethal weapons and waited in hiding for the complainant party to arrive
premeditation_planning.quote: all the accused were waiting for the complainant party to arrive at the spot
premeditation_planning.reason: Judgment describes assembly with weapons and waiting in hiding, indicating planning.

motive.quote: the accused persons intended to take revenge
motive.reason: Trial court found revenge motive tied to the way dispute and field entry.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: rightly accepted as truthful by the trial Court
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Supreme Court accepted trial court's findings on aggressors and fatal blow with intent.

witness_credibility.quote: which has been elaborately analysed and rightly accepted as truthful by the trial Court
witness_credibility.reason: Matches the judgment's assessment of prosecution witnesses.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Accused ran away after the incident once other villagers intervened
post_offence_conduct.quote: Accused persons having assumed Bhura died ran away.
post_offence_conduct.reason: Judgment states the accused ran away after the incident.

custody_duration.correct_value: About five months already undergone before the High Court's sentence
custody_duration.quote: the period already undergone (about five months)
custody_duration.reason: Judgment states the accused had undergone about five months of custody.

bail_history.correct_value: Bail bonds cancelled; accused directed to surrender to undergo remaining sentence
bail_history.reason: Judgment expressly states bail bonds were cancelled and surrender ordered.

investigation_status.quote: FIR registered on 14.8.1981 at P.S. Nagaur
investigation_status.reason: FIR date and committal in February 1982 are both stated.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Accused challenged conviction without own appeal (s.377(3) CrPC); HC judgment called cryptic
procedural_irregularity.quote: the said accused had not preferred a formal appeal against the impugned judgment
procedural_irregularity.reason: Judgment discusses a procedural point on challenging conviction without appeal and a cryptic HC judgment.

appeal_history.quote: the High Court converted the conviction under Section 302, IPC into one under Section 326, IPC
appeal_history.reason: Trial, High Court and Supreme Court outcomes are accurately summarised.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: State sought restoration of s.302 conviction and life imprisonment; argued accused were aggressors
prosecution_argument.quote: the State was pursuing this appeal only against the accused No. 5 ... for restoration of his conviction under Section 302, IPC and to award him sentence of life imprisonment
prosecution_argument.reason: State sought s.302 murder conviction, not s.304-I; the value misstates the prosecution's position.

defence_argument.correct_value: Private defence; provocation; single blow without intention to cause death; accused aged 70-75; challenge to conviction without appeal
defence_argument.quote: the incident had occurred on the spur of the moment due to provocation
defence_argument.reason: Core private defence and provocation points are right; omits age and procedural arguments, and 'free fight' is the court's finding.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Private defence unavailable where accused are aggressors; s.304 Part I applies where grave and sudden provocation and intention to cause death or bodily injury likely to cause death
legal_principle_applied.quote: the case would be covered by Section 304 Part I, IPC
legal_principle_applied.reason: Core principle is right, but 'intention to kill' misstates the s.304 Part I test and omits the provocation basis.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Chandrakant Patil v. State through CBI (1998) 3 SCC 38
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Seven precedents listed match those cited in the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.correct_value: Nature and gravity of offence and background of provocation by complainant's unauthorised entry; fatal blow on vital part
sentencing_rationale.quote: considering the nature and gravity of the offence and the background in which it is committed
sentencing_rationale.reason: Omits the provocation background, and aggressor finding was about private defence rather than sentencing.

judicial_mitigating_factors.correct_value: Grave and sudden provocation by complainant's repeated unauthorised entry on fields
judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: deprived of the power of self-control by grave and sudden provocation
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Judgment identifies grave and sudden provocation as mitigating; 'None' is wrong.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: the solitary fatal blow on the vital part of the head by accused No. 5
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Fatal blow on vital part and gravity of offence are weighed as aggravating.

other_sentence_order.quote: directed to pay compensation to the tune of Rs.50,000/- to the next of kin
other_sentence_order.reason: Compensation order and adjustment under s.428 CrPC are both stated.

trial_duration.reason: Offence date, trial, High Court and Supreme Court dates match the judgment.

legal_representation.correct_value: accused/respondent: Sushil Kumar Jain, Sr. Adv., H.D. Thanvi, Rishi Matoliya; state/appellant: Dr. Manish Singhvi, Sr. Adv., D.K. Devesh, Milind Kumar
legal_representation.quote: Dr. Manish Singhvi, Sr. Adv., D.K. Devesh, Milind Kumar, Advs. for the Appellant.
legal_representation.reason: Counsel assignments are reversed; Singhvi appeared for the State appellant.
